The Trump administration imposed financial sanctions this month on the International Criminal Court, escalating a previously announced diplomatic campaign to “dismantle” the court. 

The sanctions prohibit U.S. companies and entities from transacting with the ICC.  The Hague-based ICC seeks to investigate and prosecute those responsible for grave offenses such as genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes. It has 125 members, though dozens of governments are not parties to it, including China, India, Israel, Russia, and the United States.  

The court condemned the sanctions as an attempt to obstruct justice and intimidate those who work or cooperate with it, while foreign ministers from 8 U.S. allies released a joint statement expressing their disagreement with the U.S. decision.
